accuracy.evidence: Facts checked against NASA and ESA sources: light gathered grows with the area of the opening, so a 7 cm lens collects 7 × 7 = 49 times a 1 cm lens and a doubled width collects 4 times; a convex lens refracts and a concave mirror reflects parallel light to a focus while a flat mirror does not and a convex one diverges it; the eyepiece magnifies; twinkling is atmospheric turbulence; Hubble (launched 1990, 2.4 m mirror) orbits Earth at roughly 500 km; James Webb (launched 25 December 2021, 6.5 m mirror) orbits the Sun near L2 about 1.5 million km from Earth, about four times the Moon's distance, so the lesson does not repeat the common claim that Webb orbits Earth; Galileo observed Jupiter's four large moons in January 1610 and Newton built a reflecting telescope in 1668. Simplifications (the 'what you see' blur, four height levels) are labelled as views, not measurements.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets documented children's ideas from NASA Space Place, ESA education notes and primary science misconception lists: that a telescope's main job is to make stars bigger (Col, m7, practice p1), that space telescopes are there to be closer to the stars (Dee, m1), that telescopes do not work on Earth (Fin), that stars twinkle because they switch on and off (step 4 predict, tag flash, p5), that any mirror focuses light (flat and bulging mirrors in the lab, Hal/Gia, m2), and that Webb orbits Earth like Hubble (m5, tag air).

lab_distinct.evidence: gate_lab_distinct passed (under 30% similar to every flagship lab). Related lessons 690 Reflecting Light and 706 Light Travels in Straight Lines bounce single rays off surfaces and 574 orders the planets; this lab is about telescopes only: a width slider that reveals stars by light caught (width × width) and a faint galaxy, a draggable screen behind a thin and a fat lens with a live 'what you see' blur, a slot that takes a flat, curved-in or bulging mirror with the matching reflected rays, and a telescope lifted through layers of moving air with a twinkling star view.

lab_teaches.evidence: Stars appear one brightness group at a time as the width grows and the header shows width × width, so 'wider catches more light' is discovered before the text names it. Dragging the screen shows the rays crossing and the star view shrinking to a dot only at the focus, and the fat lens's nearer focus is found by doing. Each wrong mirror draws its own reflected rays. The star view twinkles less at each height and is steady only above the air.

predictions.evidence: Step 1 asks what a wider lens shows with 'The same stars' tempting; more stars and the galaxy then appear. Step 2 asks what a lens does to starlight with 'Goes straight on' and 'Bounces back' tempting; the rays bend and meet. Step 4 asks why stars twinkle with 'They switch on and off' tempting; the star stops twinkling only above the air, though it never stops shining.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Every distractor has its own tag: small (less light, faint stars fade), eyes (the eye's opening is under 1 cm), flat (a flat mirror cannot focus; move the eyepiece), flash and clouds (moving air, no clouds in space), mount and air (Webb is 1.5 million km away), tube and cap (they do not magnify), newton and hubble (dates 1668 and 1990 against Galileo's 1610). Lab feedback names the slip: 'Too close: the light has not met yet', 'Too far: the light met, then spread out again', 'A flat mirror ... never meets at one bright point'.

readability.evidence: learn/readability.py gives the kid text grade 2.8 (limit 6.5) and the adult text 8.1 (limit 9.5). Kid sentences are short and concrete ('Your eye has a tiny hole to let light in'); focus and eyepiece are explained when first used; precise terms (refract, concave, convex, atmosphere, magnify) are in the key idea and adult text.

no_filler.evidence: gate_content found no filler phrases. Each kid paragraph teaches one idea a lab step tests (light gathering, focus with a lens or mirror, the eyepiece, the atmosphere); the adult text gives curriculum links, the five tasks and the named mistakes; hints point back to what changed in the lab.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 360 px (Android) for every step at start, mid Show me and end. After the first pass the 'what you see' view moved to the top left so it no longer sits under the screen handle, mirror tiles grew to 62 px with 12 px labels so 'Bulging out' is not clipped, height labels start below the star view so 'Hubble's orbit' is not covered, and the footer space grows with the message. Drag handles have 56 px hit boxes and every action has a full-size button.

accessibility.evidence: gate_browser passed: axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13, every task completes with Show me, no console errors. Every canvas action has a button (Wider / Narrower lens, Screen nearer / farther, Put in the … mirror, Go higher / lower, '<name> is right'), the twinkle stops under reduced motion (a steady soft disc is drawn instead), and the aria-label is rewritten after each action with the lens width, light caught and stars shown, the screen position against the focus, the mirror and what the light does, or the height and whether the star twinkles.
